public_api_validation.correction: load_shard returns curves [73,n]; writer ragged arrays are [n,73]. Compare the same orientation.
public_api_validation.exact_count_recovery: Stored f64 curves=integer prot/sweeps, with prot<=sweeps<2**24. Rounding curves*sweeps uniquely recovers prot (error far below 0.5). A successful MC diagnostic implies tot==sweeps, enforced by the driver.

rebaseline.criterion: change <=10% seed noise for count disagreement, pKa MAE and maximum; teacher MAE drift <= seed drift

design: Explicit sum of scalar site differences; CPU scalar indexing / shared ref-Pallas two-nonzero masked differences. No version, ISA, flags, bucket or cardinality eligibility gates. Scalar CPU eager site acceptance; shared ref/Pallas skips already-rejected unchanged site proposals.
default: auto: Pallas on a supported GPU, cpu on CPU, ref otherwise

portability.pair_energy: Round each site subtraction first, then add the two scalar differences. Each masked difference has at most two nonzeros, so every reduction tree equals the scalar subtraction; equal indices cancel in their cell.
portability.current_state: cur_of selects one int32 index among zeros; no overflow or floating arithmetic. CPU direct indexing is identical.
portability.rebuild_updates: Rebuild is a sequential loop in site order. E/X row updates are elementwise with unchanged parentheses. No reduction across sites or moved rows.
portability.counts: X and flag are 0/1; counts are sequential exact integer f32 additions below 2**24, enforced by public sweep limit. Host f64 counts_to_prot reduces bounded integer counts exactly; curves/pKa use common host routines.
portability.remaining: invexp: x*x, x2*x, x2*x2 and numerator/denominator multiply-add polynomials may contract to FMAs differently; GPU division can use different approximations. Nonstandard fast-math settings can additionally reassociate scalar pair/W or E-update arithmetic; subnormal handling can differ. No runtime eligibility gates assume otherwise.
portability.unchanged_proposals: The shared-chain shortcut rejects exactly the proposals already rejected by nw==oc. RNG draws, counters and accepted E/X/current/count updates are unchanged. CPU eager evaluation has the identical logical rule.

input_policy: Saved bench/gpu/energies_gpu.npz and M6 runA labels only; seed=1 versus old seed=2; alias chain ids; 20 bench/50k + CPU5/200k on CPU; 104 L3 + 20 bench/200k Pallas.
limitations: Timings are non-exclusive Slurm allocations. The one-requested-CPU timing allocation exposes two SMT CPUs (affinity 2), as in phase 3; the CPU12 timing has affinity 12. Cross-backend agreement is measured, not a gate.
